'''Thomas Hertog''' is a Belgian cosmologist at [[KU Leuven]] university and was a key collaborator of Professor [[Stephen Hawking]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kuleuven.be/wieiswie/en/person/00010845|title=KU Leuven who's who – Thomas Hertog|website=www.kuleuven.be}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Thomas Hertog was born on 27 May 1975. He graduated [[Summa cum laude]] from [[KU Leuven]] in 1997 with an [[Master of Science|MSc]] degree in physics. He obtained his [[Master's degree]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] in [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos]] and obtained a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degree at Cambridge with a thesis on the origins of [[cosmic expansion]] under the supervision of [[Stephen Hawking]].

== Career ==
Hertog had the opportunity to conduct research with [[Stephen Hawking]] in the field of [[Inflation (cosmology)|cosmic inflation]], a branch of the [[Big Bang theory]].<ref>Dirk Draulans, Eindeloos veel heelallen, in: Knack, 4 juli 2012, p. 76 t.e.m. 80.</ref>

He then worked as a researcher at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara|University of California - Santa Barbara]] in the United States and the [[Université de Paris VII]] in France. He became a fellow at [[CERN]] in Geneva in 2005. In October 2011, Hertog was appointed professor at the Institute for Theoretical Physics at KU Leuven through the Odysseus program of the [[Flemish Government|Flemish government]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fwo.be/nl/mandaten-financiering/onderzoeksprojecten/odysseusprogramma/|title=Fonds Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek – Vlaanderen – Odysseusprogramma|website=www.fwo.be}}</ref> He leads a research group studying the relationship between the Big Bang and [[string theory]], with the idea that concepts like space and time lose their meaning. He also emphasizes [[Georges Lemaître]]'s insight that the Big Bang is central to Einstein's [[gravitational wave]]s. Hertog worked in the field of [[quantum cosmology]] and string theory with [[James Hartle]] and Stephen Hawking. In 2011, after years of research, they came to a new insight by combining the mathematics of quantum cosmology and that of string theory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cam.ac.uk/research/news/taming-the-multiverse-stephen-hawkings-final-theory-about-the-big-bang#:~:text=As%20a%20consequence%2C%20Einstein's%20theory,at%20the%20beginning%20of%20time|website=University of Cambridge|title=Taming the multiverse:Stephen Hawking's final theory about the big bang|year=2018|access-date=August 27, 2025}}</ref>  In 2018, he published 'A smooth exit from eternal inflation?' with [[Stephen Hawking]].<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/JHEP04(2018)147 | doi=10.1007/JHEP04(2018)147 | title=A smooth exit from eternal inflation? | date=2018 | last1=Hawking | first1=S. W. | last2=Hertog | first2=Thomas | journal=Journal of High Energy Physics | volume=2018 | issue=4 | page=147 | arxiv=1707.07702 | bibcode=2018JHEP...04..147H | s2cid=13745992 }}</ref>

Hertog was an important contributor to the development of [[top-down cosmology]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hawking|first1=S. W.|last2=Hertog|first2=Thomas|date=2006-06-23|title=Populating the landscape: A top-down approach|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevD.73.123527|journal=Physical Review D|volume=73|issue=12|article-number=123527|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.73.123527|arxiv=hep-th/0602091|bibcode=2006PhRvD..73l3527H|s2cid=9856127}}</ref> He explains the theory in his 2023 book [[On the Origin of Time]], which Hawking asked him to write just before his death.<ref>Hertog, Thomas. ''On the Origin of Time''. Random House, 2023, p. 248.</ref>
